ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, points $A$, $B$, and $C$ are all on the circle $\odot O$. If $\angle ACB = 36^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle OAB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\because \angle ACB=\frac{1}{2}\angle AOB$ and $\angle ACB=36^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle AOB=2\times \angle ACB=72^\circ$. \\
$\because OA=OB$, \\
$\therefore \triangle OAB$ is an isosceles triangle, \\
$\because \angle AOB+\angle OAB+\angle OBA=180^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle OAB=\frac{1}{2}\left(180^\circ−\angle AOB\right)=54^\circ$, \\
Thus, the answer is: $\boxed{54^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle with O as the center; the three points A, B, and C are all on the circumference; A is at the lower left, B is at the lower right, and C is at the upper right. In the figure, AC, BC, and AB are connected, and the center O is connected to A and B, so OA and OB are radii. ∠ACB is an inscribed angle formed by the chords CA and CB, and what it subtends is the arc/chord AB; ∠AOB is a central angle formed by the radii OA and OB, corresponding to the same arc AB. Reasoning: The central angle subtending the same arc is equal to 2 times the inscribed angle, so ∠AOB = 2 × ∠ACB = 2 × 36° = 72°. Because OA = OB, △OAB is an isosceles triangle, so ∠OAB = ∠OBA. The sum of the interior angles of a triangle is 180°, so the sum of the two base angles is 180° − 72° = 108°, and each base angle is 108° ÷ 2 = 54°. Therefore ∠OAB = 54°.
